name: MOSCAB
summary: MOSCAB studies a superheated-liquid bubble chamber with a geyser-like cycle, a self-resetting approach to low-background dark-matter detection.
detection_principle: A temperature gradient establishes superheated conditions. Particle energy deposition triggers bubbles, and evaporation/condensation restores the system, reducing the complexity of mechanical pressure cycling.

results.summary: A laboratory prototype validated the geyser operating principle; this is not a dark-matter signal.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
